verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents its own official command-line tool, `fhcli`, but the evidence describes it only as a way to submit change events (Docker image creation, Jenkins deploys, CI build statuses) from CI and orchestration systems. It does not cover broader incident, alerting or runbook management that an AI-native or agentic workflow would need. Missing for 10: evidence of broad CLI coverage of the platform (incidents, Signals, runbooks), agent-oriented or machine-readable output, install and command reference depth, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: FireHydrant provides a command line tool, `fhcli`, to easily submit changes from your existing CI or orchestration systems.
You can use fhcli to record the creation of Docker images, deploy events in Jenkins, CI build statuses, etc.
